domain: Religious Studies / Collective Memory / Ritual Practice
topic_summary: Analysis of Jewish catastrophe-commemoration rituals (Tisha B'Av, Passover) as contested kernels of mourning-practice preservation. The kernel question: does ritual transmission preserve survival-competence (adaptive capacity under persecution) or only mourning-practice itself (symbolic continuity without operational yield)?

key_entities: Tisha B'Av (annual fast commemorating Temple destructions, 586 BCE and 70 CE)
Passover (annual festival commemorating Exodus from Egypt, ~1300 BCE claimed)
Rabbinic tradition (interpretive authority grounding ritual continuity)
Historical catastrophes (Temple destructions, expulsions, pogroms, Shoah)
key_tensions: Ritual fidelity vs adaptive modification (preserve exact form vs context-responsive practice)
Mourning-as-memory vs mourning-as-preparation (symbolic continuity vs operational readiness)

axes.structural_delta: Contested readings of what ritual catastrophe-commemoration preserves across millennia
axes.primary_observable: Ritual practice continuity metrics; community survival rates under persecution; adaptive capacity indicators
axes.selection_reason: Core contested kernel with structurally distinct readings that emit different constraint types

omegas.description: Does the Shoah represent a discontinuity that invalidates pre-1945 readings? Post-Shoah theology may have generated a fifth reading (theodicy-crisis) not captured in the four-reading decomposition.

In secularized communities, does ritual practice shift from any of the four readings to pure cultural-identity marker (D1 without D4/D5 operational content)? This would reclassify the constraint type.

Do other catastrophe-commemoration traditions (Armenian Genocide remembrance, African diaspora ritual) exhibit the same reading-structure? Cross-tradition comparison may reveal whether the four-reading decomposition is tradition-specific or structurally general.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Four-reading decomposition derived from multi-lens scan (ritual studies, collective memory theory, diaspora survival analysis, halakhic jurisprudence). Each reading passes individually-holdable test and emits structurally distinct constraint.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Ritual catastrophe-commemoration as mechanism for transmitting collective memory across millennia of diaspora
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive tradition grounding ritual practice-norms; halakhic framework encoding transmission fidelity

readings.commitment: Ritual preserves symbolic continuity and collective identity across time
readings.expected_structural_delta: D1/D4 constraint: mourning-practice as identity-marker; beneficiary is tradition-continuity itself; victim is adaptive modification (ritual rigidity costs). Low extractiveness — symbolic transmission without operational survival yield.

readings.commitment: Ritual encodes and transmits adaptive capacity for persecution-survival
readings.expected_structural_delta: D5 constraint: mourning-practice as survival-training; beneficiary is community resilience under threat; victim is assimilation pressure (boundary-maintenance costs). Moderate extractiveness — operational competence preserved through ritual rehearsal of catastrophe-response patterns.

readings.commitment: Ritual encodes intergenerational trauma as warning system
readings.expected_structural_delta: D4 constraint: mourning-practice as trauma-transmission mechanism; beneficiary is threat-vigilance (early-warning capacity); victim is psychological burden on descendants. Moderate-to-high extractiveness — trauma costs imposed on future generations for collective threat-detection.

readings.commitment: Ritual enforces group boundaries through shared mourning-practice
readings.expected_structural_delta: D3 constraint: mourning-practice as boundary-enforcement; beneficiary is in-group cohesion; victim is individual autonomy and out-group relations. Moderate extractiveness — boundary-maintenance costs (exclusion, conformity pressure) for group solidarity.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Symbol-continuity reading treats operational survival-yield as epiphenomenal (ritual persists because it is tradition, not because it confers adaptive advantage). Survival-competence reading treats symbolic content as instrumental (ritual persists because it encodes survival-relevant information). No single framework holds both: either tradition-continuity is the terminal value or survival-competence is.

Trauma-encoding reading treats ritual as mechanism imposing psychological costs on descendants for collective threat-detection (extractive). Symbol-continuity reading treats ritual as cost-free identity-marker (non-extractive symbolic transmission). No single framework holds both: either the ritual extracts from future generations or it does not.
